Among the many Apple Intelligence features coming in iOS 27, the Passwords app is getting a particularly powerful capability: automatically changing your passwords for you.

iOS 27's Passwords app can fix compromised credentials on your behalf, powered by Apple Intelligence

The next generation of Apple Intelligence will be at the heart of the upcoming iOS 27 and related software updates. One of the powerful new AI features relates to Apple's Passwords app.

The Passwords app launched two years ago as a dedicated hub for logins, two-factor authentication codes, Wi-Fi passwords, passkeys, and more.

If passwords in your database have issues, the app has always alerted you. For example, if your password has appeared in a data breach or is reused across multiple accounts, Passwords will notify you.

But until now, you've still had to manually deal with these problematic credentials yourself.

However, in iOS 27, Apple says their new agentic AI capabilities can change your passwords directly in many situations. According to Apple's official website:

With this feature, you can always keep your credentials secure and use strong passwords, while minimizing the hassle and time required.

iOS 27 is currently in beta and will be released to all users in the coming weeks. The new Passwords feature is expected to ship with iOS 27.0, but availability in the beta has been unstable, so it may be delayed until iOS 27.1.

Have you tried the new Passwords feature in the iOS 27 beta? How has your experience been? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
